Στίχ. ʹ. Τὰ ἔγκατα αὐτοῦ ἀσπίδες χαλκαῖ. Τὰ δόγματα, τὰ νοήματα τὰ
ἀποκεκρυμμένα. Πάντα ἰὸς ἀσπίδων ἐστὶ, πάντα τὰ ἔνδον αὐτοῦ. Καὶ ἀσπίδες εἰσὶν
οὐχ ἁπαλαί τινες, ἀλλὰ σκληραί. Ἀσπί δες γάρ εἰσι σκληραί. Στίχ. ιʹ. Ἐκ στόματος
αὐτοῦ. Αἱ βλασφημίαι καὶ οἱ λόγοι τῶν ἀσεβῶν καὶ ἀθέων διδασκάλων. Στίχ. ιʹ. Ἐκ
στόματος αὐτοῦ ἐκπορεύονται λαμ πάδες καιόμεναι, καὶ διαριπτοῦνται ἐσχάραι
πυρός. Οἶμαι μὲν καὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς ἀθέων δογμάτων εἰσηγητὰς κυρίως ἂν
εἶναι μέλη τοῦ δρά κοντος· καὶ τῶν μελῶν τοῦ δράκοντος ὀνόματα εἰ θέλεις
ἀκοῦσαι, ποῖοί εἰσιν οὗτοι; Τὸ στόμα τοῦ δράκοντος εἴη δ' ἄν τι καὶ τροπικῶς
νοούμενον, καὶ παρὰ τοῦτο ὅθεν οἱ λόγοι οἱ ἀπολλύντες. [Ἐκ στό ματος γὰρ αὐτοῦ
λαμπάδες ἀπολλύονται πυρός.] Ὅτι ἐκ στόματος αὐτοῦ ἐσχάραι ἀπολλύονται πυρός.
Εἴ ποτε ἤκουσα τοῦ κατηγοροῦντος λόγου, προφάσει Χριστιανισμοῦ, κατηγοροῦντος
τοῦ ∆ημιουρ γοῦ, φέρε εἰπεῖν, πρεσβεύοντος τὰ Μαρκίωνος, πρε σβεύοντος τὰ
Οὐαλεντίνου, καὶ τὰ Βασιλείδου· ὅτ' ἂν κακῶς λέγωσιν τὸν Ποιητὴν οὐρανοῦ καὶ
γῆς, ὅτ' ἂν λέγωσιν αὐτὸν μὴ εἶναι, μηδὲ πνευματικῆς οὐσίας, ὁποῖά φασιν οὗτοι·
ὄψῃ, ἐκ στόματος τῶν τοιούτων ἐξέρχονται λαμπάδες καιόμεναι, καὶ διαρι πτοῦνται
ἐσχάραι πυρός. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο ἡμεῖς, εἰδότες, τηρῶμεν ἑαυτοὺς, μήποτε ἐκεῖναι αἱ
λαμπάδες ἡμᾶς καύσωσι, μήποτε αἱ ἐσχάραι τοῦ πυρὸς ἡμῶν ἅψωνται. Στίχ. ιγʹ. Ἐν
δὲ τραχήλῳ αὐτοῦ αὐλίζεται δύ ναμις. Ἔστι τις δύναμις πονηρά. Ἀλλ' ἡ ἀσθένεια, ἣν
ἀνέλαβε δι' ἐμὲ ὁ Σωτήρ μου καὶ Κύριος, ἥτις λέγε ται ἀσθένεια Θεοῦ, ἐνίκησεν
pass_a_gloss: …fear. For the Lord your God you will fear, and besides him do not fear the other. Verse (number lost). His inward parts bronze asps (shields). The doctrines, the thoughts that have been hidden. All is venom of asps, all the things within him. And they are asps not some soft ones, but hard. For asps (shields) are hard. Verse 10. From his mouth. The blasphemies and the words of the impious and atheist teachers. Verse 10. From his mouth go out lamps burning, and grates of fire are thrown about. I suppose all the impious introducers of atheist doctrines to be properly members of the dragon; and the names of the members of the dragon if you wish to hear, of what sort are these? The mouth of the dragon would be also something understood figuratively, and beside this whence the words that destroy. [For from his mouth lamps of fire perish.] That from his mouth grates of fire perish. If ever I heard the accusing speech, on pretext of Christianity, accusing the Craftsman (Creator), bring to say, championing the things of Marcion, championing the things of Valentinus, and the things of Basilides; whenever they speak badly of the Maker of heaven and earth, whenever they say him not to be, nor of spiritual substance, such things as these say: you will see, out of the mouth of such ones go out burning lamps, and grates of fire are thrown about. Through this we, knowing, let us guard ourselves, lest ever those lamps burn us, lest ever the grates of the fire touch us. Verse 13. And in his neck lodges power. There is some wicked power. But the weakness, which my Saviour and Lord took up for my sake, which is called weakness of God, conquered…
pass_b_english: … fear. For “you shall fear the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 6:13), and apart from him do not fear any other.

“His insides are bronze asps” (Job 41:15). These are his teachings, his hidden thoughts. Everything is the venom of asps, everything that is inside him. And they are not some soft asps but hard ones; for the asps are hard.
“From his mouth” (Job 41:19): the blasphemies and the words of ungodly and godless teachers.

“From his mouth go out burning torches, and braziers of fire are flung about” (Job 41:19). I think, for my part, that all the ungodly who bring in godless doctrines would properly be members of the dragon. And if you want to hear the names of the dragon's members, who are they? The dragon's mouth may also be something understood figuratively, and with it the place from which the destroying words come. [For from his mouth torches of fire perish.] Because from his mouth braziers of fire perish.

If I ever heard a speech that accused the Creator under the pretext of Christianity, a speech, say, championing the teachings of Marcion, championing those of Valentinus and of Basilides; when they speak ill of the Maker of heaven and earth, when they say that he is not, and is not of spiritual substance either, the sort of things these men say: you will see that from the mouth of such people burning torches go out and braziers of fire are flung about. That is why we, who know this, should keep watch over ourselves, so that those torches never burn us and the braziers of fire never touch us.

“And in his neck power makes its home” (Job 41:22). There is a certain wicked power. But the weakness that my Saviour and Lord took on for my sake, which is called the weakness of God, has conquered …

choices.choice: First person kept: 'I think', 'If I ever heard', 'my Saviour and Lord ... for my sake'. Third-person 'Origen takes...' removed.
Marcion, Valentinus, Basilides are named by the author himself; translated as written, no label added.
The edition's square brackets kept around 'For from his mouth torches of fire perish', and noted; ἀπολλύονται translated 'perish' as written.
Reference only on 'you shall fear the Lord your God' (Deuteronomy 6:13); the added clause 'apart from him do not fear any other' left uncited.
Stichos labels (lost numeral, ιʹ, ιγʹ) not printed; LXX/MT 41:7 = KJV 41:15; 41:11 = 41:19; 41:14 = 41:22.
